candidates.title: To Do planning and completion rely on dragging
candidates.impact: A keyboard user can edit existing hours but cannot create the ordinary planned block or move it to Done through equivalent controls.
candidates.observed: The normal working week creates blocks only when a project-card drag payload is dropped onto a To do day. The project card offers only a project-navigation link. Existing blocks expose a keyboard-openable editor for Stage/Hours/Note, with no date or To do/Done control. The Add time button occurs only in preview empty/complete states. Resize targets also have pointer-only handlers.
candidates.expected: A non-drag route supports the same core creation and completion tasks while dragging remains available.
authority: User audit scope: keyboard interaction, daily task efficiency
brisk-production-journey.md: time logging at project/Stage level
candidates.recommendation: Add a small accessible Add time entry point and expose date and completion changes through the existing contextual editor or adjacent actions. Keep drag/drop as the faster pointer shortcut.
candidates.rationale: This gives parity for core work without redesigning the working-week layout.
alternatives: A project-card Add to day menu can provide a contextual route, but avoid making every day a large new button.
candidates.tradeoffs: Decide whether Done means a completed plan or logged hours before choosing labels; preserve existing time model and role restrictions. Do not expand into a new time-tracking product.
candidates.rootCause: Drag-and-drop is the only normal creation/completion affordance.
evidence: Requested lead capture: /today normal working week and existing time editor, keyboard reachable actions without saving.
candidates.approvedReference: No approved screenshot specifies a keyboard alternative. Existing To Do visual references establish layout only.
candidates.verificationRemaining: Browser keyboard inspection pending. Creation, dragging, completion, Delete and Save must remain unsubmitted during this audit.
candidates.exclusionReason: Current captured To Do fixture is empty. Drag-only populated UI concern remains a verification question, excluded from active findings until applicable UI is observed.

candidates.title: Cancelling Staff assignment can still save edited hours
candidates.impact: A user can cancel the withdrawal/assignment confirmation while unknowingly retaining a preceding hours change.
candidates.observed: addStaff invokes onSaveSettings(draftRoleHours) before checking activeInvitations and opening the withdrawal confirmation. Cancelling that confirmation clears only staffPendingConfirmation. The parent save callback persists the redistributed hours independently.
candidates.expected: Cancel at the confirmation boundary leaves unconfirmed edits unchanged, or the UI explicitly explains which changes have already been saved.
authority: Brisk DS/guidelines/components/editing-dialog.md: preserve save boundaries and cancellation meaning
Brisk DS/guidelines/components/confirmation-dialog.md: cancel confirmation without changing data
candidates.recommendation: Defer the implicit hours save until Staff assignment is confirmed, keeping the separate explicit Save changes action intact.
candidates.rationale: This is a small ordering correction; assigning and editing role hours remain distinct actions.
alternatives: Require Save changes before assignment, but this adds friction and should be justified if chosen.
candidates.tradeoffs: Do not merge Save, Assign, Invite, Withdraw or Remove into one action; preserve pending-invitation safeguards and capacity recalculation.
candidates.rootCause: Mutation occurs before the confirmation decision.
candidates.approvedReference: No approved screenshot for this branch; the DS cancellation contract is authoritative.
candidates.verificationRemaining: Not executed because entering this confirmation after dirty hours would itself change stored hours. Source-backed review only; verify with isolated non-persisting state before implementation.
candidates.exclusionReason: Unverified source-only hours-save ordering issue removed from UI-focused recommendations under latest user steering. Retained solely as an inspection safety note.

candidates.title: To Do accepts cross-day drops without rescheduling the block
candidates.impact: If cross-day rescheduling is intended, the apparent drop target silently leaves work on its original day. Current fixture and source do not establish the intended restriction.
candidates.confidence: High about source outcome; intent unconfirmed
states: Existing time block dragged to a different weekday
candidates.observed: Every DaySection accepts time-entry drag payloads and calls onMoveEntry with its date. moveEntry changes status only when entry.date already equals the destination date; otherwise it returns the original entry. It never changes the entry date, and there is no rejection or explanation for a cross-day drop.
candidates.expected: A presented rescheduling target either moves the block to that date or explains a deliberate restriction before the user drops it.
authority: User audit scope: controls whose apparent and actual behaviour differ
Current TodayPage UI presents each weekday as a valid time-entry drop target; no approved cross-day restriction found
candidates.recommendation: Confirm cross-day rescheduling as the intended task. If allowed, update date with the destination and give brief feedback; if forbidden, make the invalid target and reason apparent.
candidates.rationale: The smallest coherent repair aligns the drag affordance and outcome rather than redesigning the calendar.
alternatives: A date field in the existing editor also supports keyboard rescheduling but does not by itself correct misleading drag targets.
candidates.tradeoffs: Keep same-day To do/Done transitions, hours, notes and viewed-person scope intact. Do not persist new planning behaviour without clarifying the prototype time model.
candidates.rootCause: The drop callback passes a date that moveEntry deliberately never assigns.
evidence: Requested current /today default screenshot; cross-day mutation not performed.
candidates.approvedReference: No approved reference establishes a cross-day restriction. No before/after evidence exists because no planning record was changed.
candidates.verificationRemaining: Source-supported only. Verify with isolated disposable planning state, then confirm actual product intent with Tom.
candidates.exclusionReason: Unverified prototype rescheduling implementation logic removed from UI-focused recommendations under latest user steering.
